thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point to Higher Open on Trade Talk Hopes; Wall Street Digests CPI Data

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point to Higher Open on Trade Talk Hopes; Wall Street Digests CPI Data
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Wednesday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +1.2%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +1.9%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +1.5%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +1.5%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -0.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 1.5%.
US stock futures were higher ahead of the open after comments from US President Donald Trump helped ease trade jitters. Trump had said in an interview with Reuters that he was willing to intervene in the arrest of Huawei's chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou if it would help finalize a trade deal with China.
Meanwhile, Meng was allowed to post bail of CAD10 million, or about $7.5 million, by a judge in the Vancouver, court, but will still be closely monitored by authorities.
In economic data news, the Labor Department said the consumer price index (CPI) for November was unchanged, in line with forecasts. Year-over-year, the CPI slowed to 2.2% from 2.5% and was near the lowest level for the year.
The core CPI reading, which excludes the volatile prices of food and energy, rose 0.2% -- also matching expectations.
Looking ahead, the Treasury Budget for November is due out at 2:00 pm ET.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were inactive.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were also quiet in pre-market trade.
Vera Bradley (VRA) fell more than 11% after the company reported Q3 non-GAAP earnings of $0.12 per share, compared with the prior-year period's $0.23 per share. Analysts polled by Capital IQ were expecting EPS of $0.16. Revenue was $97.7 million, down from $114.1 million in the same quarter last year. The Street view was for revenue of $101.7 million. The company expects Q4 EPS of $0.22 - $0.25 on revenue of $114 million - $119 million. The Street view is for EPS of $0.22 on revenue of $114.1 million. For FY18, it sees EPS of $0.57 - $0.60 on revenue of $412 million - $417 million. Analysts are looking for EPS of $0.60 on revenue of $415.9 million.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.9% in pre-market trade. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 2.4% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2.2%.
HSBC Holdings (HSBC) ADRs were up nearly 3% after the company said its Global Banking and Markets division is teaming up with Tresata to automate the creation and consumption of quality data and actionable intelligence to enhance operational management and critical decision making to better serve its customers.
According to the British lender, Tresata will deploy its advanced analytics operating system, including intelligent customer identification and predictive analytics, to identify, link and assign data across all customers before making it available to the bank's data-driven digital and analytics products and services.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rose 1.6% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) may consider moving iPhone production out of China if the US tariff on imports hits 25%, according to a report from Bloomberg. The company is planning to keep its existing Chinese production plan in place if the US imposes a 10% tariff on smartphone imports, the report said, citing unnamed sources familiar with the matter. Apple manufactures the majority of its iPhones through its assembly partner Hon Hai Precision Industry in China. AAPL shares rose 0.7%.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was quiet and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 1.4% in pre-market trade.
Nordic American Offshore (NAO) said that it has received a $5 million investment from Scorpio Offshore Investments in the form of a private placement of common shares at $0.42 apiece. Upon closing of the private placement, Emanuele Lauro, the founder and CEO of Scorpio Tankers, will become the company's CEO. Cameron Mackey, Scorpio's chief operating officer, will become Nordic American's COO.
Commodities
Crude was up 2%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 1.7%. Natural gas was down 3.4% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 2.6%.
Gold was up 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.2%. Silver was up 0.8%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.7%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were flat in pre-market trade. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.8%.
Mallinckrodt (MNK) fell nearly 8% as the company said a reformulation of its painkiller Roxicodone failed to win approval from the US Food and Drug Administration. The company said its SpecGx subsidiary received a complete response letter from the FDA on its new drug application for its abuse-deterrent, immediate-release reformulation of Roxicodone. The FDA identified areas where further evaluation is necessary, the company said. Mallinckrodt said it will continue to pursue a pathway to try to gain approval of the drug. The company was seeking approval for the drug to be used in the treatment of certain types of pain severe enough to require an opioid and for which other treatments are inadequate.
